questions.q: What is a magnetic field line?
questions.a: An imaginary curve whose tangent at a point gives the direction of the magnetic field there.

questions.q: State two properties of magnetic field lines.
questions.a: They leave the north pole and enter the south pole outside the magnet, and never intersect each other.

questions.q: Why do two field lines never cross?
questions.a: At a crossing point the compass needle would have to point in two directions at once, which is impossible.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field of a Straight Conductor

solution_steps.name: field_units
solution_steps.explain: field strength near the wire grows with current and falls with distance

solution_steps.name: field_at_half_distance
solution_steps.explain: halving the distance doubles the field strength

questions.q: A straight wire carries 5 A. Taking the field measure as current divided by distance, find its value at 0.2 m, and at half that distance.
questions.a: 50 units

questions.q: A 6 A wire is probed at 0.3 m. Compute the field measure and its value at 0.15 m.
questions.a: 40 units

questions.q: Find the field measure (current/distance) for 9 A at 0.6 m from a long straight conductor.
questions.a: 30 units

questions.q: At 0.8 m from a 4 A wire, evaluate the field measure and the doubled value at 0.4 m.
questions.a: 10 units

questions.q: A 10 A cable is measured 2.5 m away. What is the field measure there?
questions.a: 8 units

questions.q: State the right-hand thumb rule.
questions.a: Hold the wire with the right hand, thumb along the current; the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field around the wire.

questions.q: What happens to the field around a straight wire if the current reverses?
questions.a: The direction of the circular field around the wire also reverses.

questions.q: How does the magnetic field near a straight current-carrying wire depend on distance?
questions.a: The field strength decreases as we move away from the wire - concentric circles get farther apart.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field of a Circular Loop

solution_steps.name: total_field
solution_steps.explain: each loop of the coil adds the same field at the centre

questions.q: A circular coil of 100 turns has a centre field of 0.8 units per turn. What is the total field?
questions.a: 80 units

questions.q: A loop of 50 turns contributes 1.2 units per turn at the centre. Find the total.
questions.a: 60 units

questions.q: For a 200-turn coil with 0.5 units per turn, compute the total field at the centre.
questions.a: 100 units

questions.q: A coil of 75 turns gives 0.4 units per turn. What is the combined field?
questions.a: 30 units

questions.q: If each of 120 turns adds 2 units, what total field results at the coil centre?
questions.a: 240 units

questions.q: What is a solenoid?
questions.a: A coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped in the shape of a cylinder.

questions.q: Why does a current-carrying solenoid behave like a bar magnet?
questions.a: Its field pattern is the same as a bar magnet's: one end acts north, the other south.

questions.q: How can the field inside a solenoid be made stronger?
questions.a: Increase the current, increase the number of turns per length, or put a soft iron core inside.

concepts.title: Force on a Conductor in a Magnetic Field

questions.q: When does a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field move?
questions.a: When current flows through it at an angle to the field, a force (motor principle) acts on the conductor.

questions.q: On what factors does the force on a conductor in a magnetic field depend?
questions.a: The strength of the magnetic field, the current, and the length of the conductor within the field.

questions.q: Which rule gives the direction of this force?
questions.a: Fleming's left-hand rule.

questions.q: State Fleming's left-hand rule.
questions.a: With forefinger, middle finger and thumb of the left hand at right angles: field along forefinger, current along middle finger, force (motion) along thumb.

questions.q: What is the working principle of an electric motor?
questions.a: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences forces in opposite directions on its sides, rotating it; a commutator keeps the rotation going.

questions.q: In an electric motor, what is the role of the split ring?
questions.a: The split-ring commutator reverses the current in the coil every half turn so the coil keeps spinning one way.

questions.q: What is the standard potential difference of domestic supply in India?
questions.a: 220 V alternating current at 50 Hz.

questions.q: Why are household appliances connected in parallel?
questions.a: Each appliance gets the full 220 V, can be switched independently, and one failing does not stop the others.

questions.q: Name the two wires of a domestic circuit and their colours.
questions.a: Live wire with red insulation and neutral wire with black insulation; an earth wire (green) connects metal bodies to ground.

questions.q: What is overloading of a circuit?
questions.a: Connecting appliances that draw more current than the wiring can safely carry, overheating it.

questions.q: What is a short circuit?
questions.a: Live and neutral wires touch directly, giving a very low resistance path and a sudden huge current.

questions.q: How does a fuse protect a circuit?
questions.a: The fuse wire melts when current exceeds its rating, breaking the circuit before damage occurs.
